items.title: US inmate Christa Pike says she woke up 'confused and in pain' after failed execution
items.description: It is Pike's first public statement since she survived an execution attempt by lethal injection in September.

items.title: Ceasefire allows evacuation from devastated Russian-occupied Oleshky
items.description: But several hundred people are understood to have decided to stay in the frontline town, despite the lack of gas, electricity and running water.

items.title: Prominent Russian newspaper shuts down under pressure from authorities
items.description: Novaya Gazeta has been one of the most high-profile independent news outlets in Russia over the last three decades.

items.title: Spain transport minister says he won't resign over high-speed rail disaster
items.description: Óscar Puente has been facing calls to resign after two high-speed trains collided earlier in the week, killing at least 69 people.

items.title: Pope Leo XIV becomes first pontiff to vote in a US election
items.description: The Chicago-born pontiff, who has a tense relationship with Trump, mailed in a ballot for the midterm elections that will decide control of the US Congress.

items.title: US tech stocks see sharp falls over AI cost fears
items.description: Shares in Intel continue to fall while the tech-heavy Nasdaq opens at its lowest level in more than two months.

items.title: Democratic senator blames Egypt press crackdown on US military aid decision
items.description: Chris Murphy said waiving a human rights condition on aid paved the way for arrests of journalists.
